tisanes.title: Understanding Herbal Tea and Tisanes
tisanes.intro: Herbal teas, also called tisanes, are infusions of herbs, roots, flowers, seeds and spices rather than the leaves of the tea plant.
tisanes.body: Because they contain no tea leaves, herbal infusions are naturally free from caffeine and tannin. That makes them easy to enjoy in the morning, after a meal or in the evening, plain or with milk, much as you would drink your everyday chai.

herbs.title: Exploring Traditional Herbs
herbs.intro: Tulsi, ginger, cinnamon, cardamom and liquorice root have flavoured Indian kitchens for generations.
herbs.body: Many of the herbs in our blends are familiar from Indian cooking and from Ayurveda's long tradition of herbal knowledge. Each of our teas lists its herbs on the pack, so you always know what goes into your cup.

routine.title: Making Herbal Infusions Part of Your Daily Routine
routine.intro: A warm cup is a simple way to pause. Use one spoon of tea for one cup and brew it the way you like.
routine.body: Bring water to the boil, add a spoonful of your chosen blend and let it simmer for a few minutes. Add milk and sweetener if you like, strain, and take a quiet moment for yourself. Swapping one cup of black tea a day is an easy place to start.
